default.title: Try Python
default.instructions: Write some Python code and click Run.

debug01.title: Debug 1
debug01.instructions: This program contains a mistake. Run it, read the error message carefully, and fix the program.
debug01.hint: Look carefully at the names used in the program.

debug02.title: Debug 2
debug02.instructions: Run the code and read the error? Can you spot what's wrong?
debug02.hint: Check that everything that you open is also closed...

debug03.title: Debug 3
debug03.instructions: This program contains a mistake. Run it, read the error message carefully, and fix the program.
debug03.hint: Count the brackets. Does every opening bracket have a matching closing bracket?

debug04.title: Debug 4
debug04.instructions: This program contains a mistake. Run it, read the error message carefully, and fix the program.
debug04.hint: Some words are reserved by Python and can't be used as variable names.

debug05.title: Debug 5
debug05.instructions: This program contains a mistake involving data types. Run it and use the error message to help find the problem.
debug05.code:
age = 14
print("Next year you will be " + age + 1)
debug05.hint: Look at the types of the things being joined together.

debug06.title: Debug 6
debug06.instructions: This program contains a mistake. Run it, read the error message carefully, and fix the program.
debug06.hint: Check that every string starts and ends with a matching quote mark.

debug07.title: Debug 7
debug07.instructions: This program contains a mistake. Run it, read the error message carefully, and fix the program.
debug07.hint: When print() has more than one item, they need something between them.

debug08.title: Debug 8
debug08.instructions: This program contains a mistake. Run it, read the error message carefully, and fix the program.
debug08.hint: Variable names aren't allowed to start with certain characters.

debug09.title: Debug 9
debug09.instructions: This program contains a mistake. Run it, read the error message carefully, and fix the program.
debug09.hint: A string needs to start and end with the same type of quote mark.

debug10.title: Debug 10
debug10.instructions: This program contains a mistake. Run it, read the error message carefully, and fix the program.
debug10.hint: Python cares about spaces at the start of a line. Only indent when it's expected.

debug11.title: Debug 11
debug11.instructions: This program contains a mistake. Run it, read the error message carefully, and fix the program.
debug11.code:
colours = ["red", "green", "blue"]
for colour in colours
    print(colour)
debug11.hint: Every for loop line needs to end with a colon.

debug12.title: Debug 12
debug12.instructions: This program contains a mistake. Run it, read the error message carefully, and fix the program.
debug12.hint: The lines inside a loop need to be indented.

debug13.title: Debug 13
debug13.instructions: This program contains a mistake. Run it, read the error message carefully, and fix the program.
debug13.code:
pets = ["cat", "dog"]
for pet in pets:
    print(pet)
     print("Woof")
debug13.hint: Make sure every line inside the loop is indented by the same amount.

debug14.title: Debug 14
debug14.instructions: This program contains a mistake. Run it, read the error message carefully, and fix the program.
debug14.hint: A for loop needs the word 'in' between the variable and the list.

debug15.title: Debug 15
debug15.instructions: This program contains a mistake. Run it, read the error message carefully, and fix the program.
debug15.hint: You don't need an equals sign here — think about what word links the variable to the list.

debug16.title: Debug 16
debug16.instructions: This program contains a mistake. Run it, read the error message carefully, and fix the program.
debug16.hint: Check how many items are actually in the list compared with how many times the loop runs.

debug17.title: Debug 17
debug17.instructions: This program contains a mistake. Run it, read the error message carefully, and fix the program.
debug17.hint: The last valid index is one less than the length of the list.

debug18.title: Debug 18
debug18.instructions: This program contains a mistake. Run it, read the error message carefully, and fix the program.
debug18.hint: Check the spelling of the variable each time you use it.

debug19.title: Debug 19
debug19.instructions: This program contains a mistake. Run it, read the error message carefully, and fix the program.
debug19.hint: Check the spelling of the list name in the for loop.

debug20.title: Debug 20
debug20.instructions: This program contains a mistake. Run it, read the error message carefully, and fix the program.
debug20.hint: Remember that list indexes start counting from 0, not 1.

debug21.title: Debug 21
debug21.instructions: This program should print the area of a rectangle that is 5 by 3. It should print 'The area is 15' but it doesn't. Run it, then fix the mistake.
debug21.code:
length = 5
width = 3
area = length + width
print(f"The area is {area}")
debug21.hint: To find the area of a rectangle, you multiply the length and width, not add them.

debug22.title: Debug 22
debug22.instructions: This program should work out the cost of 3 items at $5 each and print 'Total cost: 15'. Run it and see what it prints instead, then fix the mistake.
debug22.code:
price = "5"
quantity = 3
total = price * quantity
print(f"Total cost: {total}")
debug22.hint: Check whether price is stored as a number or as text. Only numbers can be multiplied together properly.

debug23.title: Debug 23
debug23.instructions: This program should say that someone who is 14 now will be 15 next year. Run it, then fix the mistake.
debug23.code:
age = 14
next_year_age = age + 2
print(f"Next year you will be {next_year_age}")
debug23.hint: Think carefully about how many years pass between now and 'next year'.

debug24.title: Debug 24
debug24.instructions: This program should print the average of 10 and 20, which is 15. Run it and see what it prints instead, then fix the mistake.
debug24.code:
a = 10
b = 20
average = a + b / 2
print(f"The average is {average}")
debug24.hint: Python calculates division before addition. You may need brackets to control the order things happen in.

debug25.title: Debug 25
debug25.instructions: This program should take $10 off a $50 item and print 'Sale price: 40'. Run it, then fix the mistake.
debug25.code:
original_price = 50
discount = 10
sale_price = original_price + discount
print(f"Sale price: {sale_price}")
debug25.hint: A discount should make the price go down, not up.

debug26.title: Debug 26
debug26.instructions: This program should print 'My favourite colour is blue', since "blue" is the third colour in the list. Run it, then fix the mistake.
debug26.code:
colours = ["red", "green", "blue"]
favourite = colours[0]
print(f"My favourite colour is {favourite}")
debug26.hint: Remember that list positions start counting from 0, so the first item is at position 0.

debug27.title: Debug 27
debug27.instructions: This program should print 'Average score: 4.5' for a total of 9 marks over 2 tests. Run it and see what it prints instead, then fix the mistake.
debug27.code:
total_marks = 9
number_of_tests = 2
average = total_marks // number_of_tests
print(f"Average score: {average}")
debug27.hint: The // operator rounds division down to a whole number. Is that the operator you want here?

debug28.title: Debug 28
debug28.instructions: This program should convert 20 degrees Celsius to Fahrenheit and print '20C is 68.0F'. Run it, then fix the mistake.
debug28.hint: The full formula is (celsius times 9/5) plus 32. Check whether every part of the formula is there.

debug29.title: Debug 29
debug29.instructions: This program should add the price of an apple ($2) and a banana ($3) and print 'Total cost: 5'. Run it, then fix the mistake.
debug29.code:
apple_price = 2
banana_price = 3
total = apple_price + apple_price
print(f"Total cost: {total}")
debug29.hint: Look closely at the variable names being added together. Are they the right ones?

debug30.title: Debug 30
debug30.instructions: This program should print 'You scored 90.0%' for a mark of 18 out of 20. Run it and see what it prints instead, then fix the mistake.
debug30.code:
mark = 18
total = 20
percentage = mark / total
print(f"You scored {percentage}%")
debug30.hint: To turn a fraction into a percentage, what do you need to multiply it by?

debug31.title: Debug 31
debug31.instructions: The voting age is 18. This program should print 'You can vote' for someone who is 18. Run it, then fix the mistake.
debug31.hint: Should someone who is exactly 18 be allowed to vote? Check which comparison operator includes that age.

debug32.title: Debug 32
debug32.instructions: The pass mark for this test is 50. This program should print 'Pass' for a score of exactly 50. Run it, then fix the mistake.
debug32.hint: A score equal to the pass mark should still count as a pass. Which comparison operator includes 'equal to'?

debug33.title: Debug 33
debug33.instructions: Tuesday (22 degrees) was warmer than Monday (18 degrees), so this program should print 'The warmer day was Tuesday'. Run it, then fix the mistake.
debug33.code:
monday_temp = 18
tuesday_temp = 22
if monday_temp > tuesday_temp:
    warmer_day = "Tuesday"
else:
    warmer_day = "Monday"
print(f"The warmer day was {warmer_day}")
debug33.hint: Look at what each branch stores in warmer_day. Have the two day names been swapped?

debug34.title: Debug 34
debug34.instructions: The bus has a capacity of 10 people. This program should print 'Bus is full' when there are exactly 10 people on board. Run it, then fix the mistake.
debug34.hint: The bus should count as full once people reaches the capacity, not only when it goes over. Which operator includes 'equal to'?

debug35.title: Debug 35
debug35.instructions: 0 degrees is the freezing point, so this program should print 'It is freezing' when the temperature is 0. Run it, then fix the mistake.
debug35.hint: A temperature of exactly 0 should still count as freezing. Which comparison operator includes 'equal to'?

debug36.title: Debug 36
debug36.instructions: There are 8 oranges and 5 apples, so this program should print 'There are more oranges'. Run it, then fix the mistake.
debug36.code:
apples = 5
oranges = 8
if apples > oranges:
    more_fruit = "apples"
else:
    more_fruit = "apples"
print(f"There are more {more_fruit}")
debug36.hint: Look at both branches of the if statement. Do they store different results, or the same one?

debug37.title: Debug 37
debug37.instructions: This program should work out the largest of two numbers, 7 and 3, and print 'The largest number is 7'. Run it, then fix the mistake.
debug37.code:
a = 7
b = 3
if a < b:
    largest = a
else:
    largest = b
print(f"The largest number is {largest}")
debug37.hint: Think about which comparison operator you need to find the bigger number, not the smaller one.

debug38.title: Debug 38
debug38.instructions: Customers who spend $100 or more should get a discount. This program should print 'You get a discount' for someone who spent $150. Run it, then fix the mistake.
debug38.hint: Should a customer who spent more than $100 get the discount? Check which comparison operator you actually need.

debug39.title: Debug 39
debug39.instructions: This program should greet someone called Sam Lee and print 'Hello, Sam Lee'. Run it, then fix the mistake.
debug39.hint: Check the order the variables are used in inside the f-string.

debug40.title: Debug 40
debug40.instructions: A basket can hold a maximum of 5 items. This program should print 'Basket is full' when there are exactly 5 items in it. Run it, then fix the mistake.
debug40.hint: The basket should count as full once it reaches the maximum, not only when it goes over. Which operator includes 'equal to'?
